I'm probably missing something, but this site's missing a distinction from Reddit, despite being a blatant clone.

Sure, it has the privacy thing, but Reddit has that too. They've released a transparency report and seem pretty uptight about fighting any claims. Email isn't required on Reddit; it's optional. In other words, the privacy issue is a rout.

Instead of distinguishing itself openly in a meaningful way, it plays the 'any resemblances are entirely incidental' card. It doesn't pose as an ethical alternative or give any justification for using it over a competitor. I suspect that there are justifications, as a fair few people seem to be jumping ship, but they aren't prominently displayed anywhere. This seems like an error, considering that the majority of users will be those seeking a Reddit alternative.

One reason given in the other thread I made in /v/introductions is the smaller site-wide community. This makes sense. Is being smaller the only thing this place has going for it?
Check the post you made an hour ago
I did. I also mentioned it in this thread OP. I created this one because of feedback instructing me to in that thread.

Unfortunately, the small community is a blessing and a curse. You see, most of the people here now are only here due to fallout from a particular event on reddit. As such, many (most?) of them have that outrage that prompted them to use this site in common and fall within the requisite demographic. Therefore, even if you're in the "in" group, since the community is so small and voting is limited for most, the quality content rarely actually shows, and instead you see the same stuff regurgitated you've probably already seen if you use reddit, but this time without the righteous indignation of naming it an actual repost. This is fine and expected, of course, as any popular Internet forum basically works this way. On the other hand, the very same userbase needed to generate the kick-ass content is turned off by feeling the thing you felt when you made this post. Namely, "why use this site when that other site already exists [and has orders of magnitude more users generating more stuff with more diversity and more variety while having no meaningful reason to stop using it]?"

tl;dr - The reason is that it's not reddit.
